{"lineage":"original","name":"The agent finds out what LENS the reader brings, and speaks in that person's vocabulary — unasked, and without ever making them ask for it","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"Anthony, 2026-08-18, promoted from `dec:idea-a-user-carries-a-persona-that-shapes-every-reply` on his instruction *"do the where-am-i fix and add the who are you ask"*, and SHARPENED the same day (see clause 1). Raised from Alex's field report that he was about to show reflow2 to coworkers and expected them to meet reflow2's own vocabulary cold. **That Decision asks WHETHER a stored persona is the right mechanism and stays open; this states WHAT IS OWED.**

WHAT IS REQUIRED, in three parts:

1. **THE AGENT ESTABLISHES WHAT LENS THE READER BRINGS, BEFORE IT READS THE DESIGN BACK — AND THE QUESTION MUST ELICIT A BACKGROUND, NOT AN IDENTITY.**

   ⭐⭐ **THIS CLAUSE WAS SHARPENED BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION FAILED ON ITS OWN TERMS.** It specified the wording *"who am I talking to, and what do you work in?"* — and Anthony caught it immediately: *"a user could reply with 'Bob' and that doesn't tell you much about Bob and the lens with which he sees his design."* **"Bob" is a correct answer to that question.** A requirement that names a question which a useless answer satisfies has not stated what it wants. **What is owed is the VOCABULARY THE READER ALREADY OWNS**, and the wording is a means to it — so this requirement states the property and leaves the phrasing to the skill.

   Three obligations follow, and they are separable:
   (a) **ASK FOR BACKGROUND, NOT IDENTITY** — what they do day to day AND what they trained in.
   (b) **SHOW WHAT A USEFUL ANSWER LOOKS LIKE.** An example in the question shapes the reply far more reliably than an instruction to answer fully. *"Software engineer, but my degree is in biology"* is the shape being asked for.
   (c) **A THIN ANSWER GETS ONE FOLLOW-UP AND NO MORE.** This is an opening courtesy, not an intake form; interrogating someone about themselves before answering their question is worse than pitching it slightly wrong.

   ⭐ **THE TWO HALVES DIVERGE, AND THE DIVERGENCE IS THE INFORMATIVE PART.** Measured against the two real users: Alex is a **software applications engineer with a bachelor's in BIOLOGY**; Anthony **develops software but came through space acquisitions and systems engineering, with a BS in EE and an MS in EE (electro-optics) focused on space object detection.** Neither is recoverable from a job title, and each changes which explanation lands — living-systems analogies for one, requirements/cost/risk and a physical signal-versus-noise intuition for the other. **A job title alone would have produced the same register for both, and it would have been wrong for both.**

2. **THE ANSWER SHAPES THE REGISTER OF EVERY REPLY, NOT ONLY OF QUESTIONS.** `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading` already governs how a CHOICE is put to the user. This covers status readouts, gap lists, explanations of what was built — the replies containing no decision at all, which is most of them.

3. **AND IT NEVER SHAPES THE RECORD.** What is written into the design stays in its own register whoever is in the room, because the next reader is someone else. `second-person-to-him-third-person-in-the-record` is the existing statement of the same split.

⭐⭐ **THE LOAD-BEARING DISTINCTION: THIS IS A VOCABULARY SWAP, NOT A DIFFICULTY DIAL.** Anthony's SE terms — requirement, interface, allocation, verification, TRL, KPP, signal-to-noise — are NATIVE and softening them patronises him and loses precision; what he wants dropped is **reflow2's INTERNAL vocabulary** (gap, loop, detector, node id, "the loop owes"). Alex's coworkers meet all of it cold. A hitting coach who knows baseball and not software wants the whole thing in terms he already owns. **None of the three wants "simpler English"; each wants a DIFFERENT vocabulary, and only one wants less technical density.** So a plain-language mode or a reading-level setting would be wrong for the primary user, wrong for the coach, and only accidentally right for a generic newcomer.

📌 **THE BACKGROUND IS A STARTING POINT, NOT A VERDICT.** People show their vocabulary by using it. When the reader's own words say more than their opening answer did, the record is updated — a background written once and never revisited goes stale like any other fact.

📌 WHERE IT IS ASKED: `where-am-i` already fires *"at the start of any session on an existing design"*, so it is the one moment reliably reached before the agent starts talking, and it is what a NEW person hits first.

🛑 **AND THAT SKILL HARDCODED AN AUDIENCE, WHICH WAS A DEFECT ON ITS OWN.** It read *"Write it as prose for the person who described this project to you"* — assuming the reader had briefed the agent. Alex's coworkers briefed nobody. Fixed 2026-08-18 (PR #246).

⚠️ **ASKING WHO SOMEBODY IS DOES NOT VIOLATE `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user`.** That decision forbids making the user choose an INTERNAL CATEGORY — a question about reflow2's schema only reflow2 can answer. Asking about their background asks for the one fact reflow2 genuinely cannot look up. **They are opposites: one hands reflow2's work to the user, the other asks for what only the user has.**

⚠️ **A GUESS IS OFFERED, NEVER ASSUMED.** A login name, a git author or an existing handle is a reasonable offer and a terrible silent default — `req:defaults-do-not-assert`. A description somebody did not choose is a stereotype the design then repeats back forever, and SELF-DESCRIBED vs ASSIGNED is the difference between a good feature and a bad one. **Live instance: Alex's background is recorded RELAYED BY ANTHONY and says so on its face, awaiting his own correction.**

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT REQUIRED, and left open in the Decision this was promoted from: a dedicated persona property on Contributor. `description` carries it today and the trial is reversible; by Anthony's own ruling (`chg:bl179-maturity-profile`) a field no computation reads does not earn its keep. ⭐ **The honest route to earning it is `ver:gap-carries-a-reading`'s `skill_lint`, which ALREADY checks that no served skill hardcodes an ANSWER LANGUAGE — the sibling check, that no served skill hardcodes an AUDIENCE, would make this mechanically enforced rather than instruction-only.**

🛑 UNTIL THAT CHECK EXISTS THIS IS AN INSTRUCTION WITH NOTHING ABLE TO OBSERVE IT — the failure `dec:idea-the-enum-question-came-back-four-days-after-it-was-fixed` measured recurring within four days of a fix shipping. Stated plainly so this is not mistaken for delivered when the prose lands.","status":"accepted"}
